title: Adding a terminal shell command requires script, VM install, and PosthogCommands changes together
answers: How do I add a new command to the PostHog terminal?
Why is my new terminal command not found in the shell?
body:
A shell-level terminal command like `open` touches several files that must stay in sync:
- `frontend/src/scenes/terminal/terminalCommands.ts`: define the sh script (e.g. OPEN_SCRIPT) and register it with `filesystem.text('open', filesystem.directory('bin', ...))` in TerminalCommands.
- `frontend/src/scenes/terminal/terminalRuntime.ts`: add a `cp /posthog/bin/<name> /usr/bin/<name> && chmod +x` line to the boot commands, otherwise the VM shell cannot find it.
- `frontend/src/scenes/terminal/posthogCommands.ts`: `PosthogCommands.execute` handles the `ph <name>` subcommand; add it to the `help` text too.
- `frontend/src/scenes/terminal/posthogFilesystem.ts`: update the README/help text shown in the terminal (usage docs live there, not in handbook docs).
The shell wrapper resolves the path with `realpath` and calls `ph <cmd>`, so symlinks are resolved in the VM before the browser sees them.
applies: frontend/src/scenes/terminal — adding or changing shell commands
